bootstrap.auto-fail-sins-evaluator:
- Displaying chord sheets with ChordSheetJS `HtmlDivFormatter`/`HtmlTableFormatter` instead of `packages/chord-render` (ChordSheetJS is allowed for parsing/serialization only)
- Chord positions stored or computed as visual columns / pixel offsets instead of grapheme indices into the logical lyric (B2)
- Flex or inline-block "chunk" layout for lines mixing strong RTL and LTR text (B3)
- Physical CSS direction properties (left/right, margin-left, text-align:left …) anywhere in styles
- Niqqud stripped from stored lyrics (strip only in `*_norm` columns)
- `packages/chord-core` or `packages/chord-render` importing `@tauri-apps/*`
- ChordPro canonical text altered or lost on save/load; derived tables treated as truth
- Copyrighted lyrics/chords in repo, fixtures, screenshots or seed DB; any network fetch of lyrics; files under `samples/` without a `samples/LICENSES.md` entry
- Song content injected via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`
- Tests touching the real user database, home directory or network; tests that assert nothing
bootstrap.auto-fail-sins-qa:
- A chord renders above the wrong grapheme in an RTL or mixed-direction line
- A chord symbol is mirrored or reordered (`#F`, `(5b)`, `7mA`)
- English word order inside a Hebrew line is broken ("rock and roll" must read LTR)
- Niqqud detached from its base letter or rendered with wrong mark positions
- Hebrew UI not mirrored (`<html dir>` not rtl, sidebar not on the right)
- Errors in the webview console during the evidenced flow
- Save reports success but stored ChordPro differs; raw Rust panic shown to the user
- Evidence captured in only one engine for a rendering change (Chromium and WebKit both required)
bootstrap.auto-fail-triggers: ChordSheetJS HtmlDivFormatter/HtmlTableFormatter used for display; chord positions stored as visual columns instead of grapheme indices; flex/inline-block chunk layout on mixed-direction lines; physical left/right CSS properties; niqqud dropped from stored lyrics (strip only in *_norm); chord-core/chord-render importing Tauri; ChordPro round-trip break; network fetch of lyrics or copyrighted text in repo/fixtures; tests hitting the real DB/home/network; weak tests / Chord over the wrong grapheme in RTL or mixed lines; chord symbol mirrored (e.g. '#F', '(5b)'); English word order broken inside a Hebrew line; niqqud detached or mis-rendered; UI chrome not mirrored in Hebrew (sidebar not on the right); webview console errors; save-without-effect; raw Rust panic shown; single-engine evidence for rendering changes

bootstrap.greenfield-practices: New behavior is developed test-first — a failing test is written before the production code that satisfies it — and modules follow SOLID: one reason to change per unit, dependencies declared against ports/abstractions rather than concretions, and no god-files that accumulate unrelated responsibilities. Pure domain modules never import UI or platform code; platform access goes through a narrow port so it can be swapped or mocked. These are authoring conventions for a fresh codebase, not evaluator auto-fail triggers.

bootstrap.models-map-caveats:
- **Anthropic-only harness**: no cross-family model is reachable from Claude Code, so fix cycle 2 and the rung-5 arbiter are same-family. Escalate repeated same-shaped failures to a human sooner. Adding Copilot or Codex as a second harness would provide cross-family models.
- **Version floors**: pins require Claude Code ≥ 2.1.293 (Haiku 5.5 is the highest floor). Run `claude update` on any machine (Ubuntu or Windows) below that.
- **Nesting depth**: `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH=3` is pinned in `.claude/settings.json`.

tokens.STACK_SUMMARY: Shir is an offline-first Hebrew + English guitar chord desktop app for Ubuntu 22.04+ and Windows 10/11: a pnpm monorepo with a Tauri 2 shell in `apps/desktop` (Rust in `src-tauri/`, React 19 + TypeScript strict + Vite UI in `src/`, Zustand, i18next en/he). Song semantics live in framework-free packages: `packages/chord-core` (ChordSheetJS 18.x for parsing/serialization plus own transposer, capo, importer and bidi line model) and `packages/chord-render` (own React renderer applying bidi rules B1–B10); neither may import any Tauri API, so an Electron fallback replaces only the shell. SQLite via rusqlite (bundled, FTS5) stores canonical ChordPro text; section/line/chord_position are derived caches rebuilt on save; typed IPC bindings come from tauri-specta. All song content is user-supplied — no lyric fetching, no copyrighted fixtures.
